questions.prompt: With maxInline 8000 and keep 2000, a command prints 50,000 characters. How many characters does the omitted-note report?
questions.explanation: The first 2,000 and last 2,000 characters are kept, so 50,000 minus 4,000 leaves 46,000 omitted.

questions.prompt: Why does the listener keep both the start and the end of the output?
options: The start usually says what the output is, and the end usually holds the error or summary
Because the model cannot read the middle of any file
To make the result exactly 4,000 characters for every tool
Because the event log only stores the first and last lines
questions.explanation: The head identifies the output and the tail tends to contain the failure or result, so together they are the most useful small slice.

questions.prompt: Why is the spill file named after the call's id?
options: So the model can guess the name without being told
Because ids are shorter than tool names
So the file is deleted when the turn ends
So two large results never overwrite each other and each can be found again
questions.explanation: Every call has a unique id, so each saved output gets its own file that matches the call in the log.
